newsitem.title: USA: Rangel says Clinton needs more fast-track support.
newsitem.headline: Rangel says Clinton needs more fast-track support.

text.p: President Clinton will have to make an effort to get more congressional Democrats to support the "fast-track" authority he wants for trade agreements, Rep. Charles Rangel, a New York Democrat, said Wednesday.

"I think the president is going to really have to start working on the Democrats to get a sufficient number of votes to get it," Rangel, the ranking Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, told reporters.

Clinton has called on Congress to give him so-called fast-track authority to negotiate a trade agreement to bring Chile into the North American Free Trade Agreement which currently links the United States, Mexico and Canada.
The authority would give Clinton the power to conclude a trade agreement with Chile that Congress could vote for or against but would not be able to slow down with amendments.

"To do this while we're going through taxes and while we're going through the budget I think would be too much for the president to carry during the same window," Rangel said, adding that he believed fast-track authority would be tackled after dealing with budget issues.
